blurb: Long-coated 'lion dog' toy breed treasured at the Chinese imperial court
description: The Shih Tzu is a small, sturdy toy breed of Tibetan and Chinese heritage, with a long double coat, a short muzzle and a lion-like look prized by royalty.
answer: The Shih Tzu is a toy breed of Tibetan origin, believed to descend from the Pekingese and Lhasa Apso, and long kept by the Chinese royal court. Its name comes from the Mandarin word for lion. It is a sturdy little dog standing no more than about 27 cm, with a long, flowing double coat.

body: The Shih Tzu was a favorite of Chinese royalty during the Ming Dynasty, and Empress Dowager Cixi ran a breeding program for it. Whether the breed should be called Tibetan or Chinese is a matter of historical and political debate. In modern Mandarin it is usually called the Xi Shi dog.

Lady Brownrigg brought the first two dogs to England in 1928, and the Shih Tzu Club wrote the first European standard in 1935. The Kennel Club recognized the breed in 1940 and the American Kennel Club in 1969. The FCI places it among the Tibetan breeds in its Companion and Toy Dog Group.

The Shih Tzu is sturdy and small, with a short snout, large dark eyes, floppy ears covered in long hair and a plumed tail carried curled over the back. An underbite is required by the breed standard. The soft, long double coat may be any color; white with grey blazes is often seen. A white patch on the top of the head is known in legend as the Star of Buddha.

The Wikipedia source gives little detail on temperament. The breed is generally kept as a companion or pet dog, and character is best judged in the individual dog; prospective owners often consult breed club descriptions.

The long coat tangles and mats easily and should be brushed at least every two or three days. Hair also grows in the ears, so regular ear cleaning is noted as important to prevent recurring infections. Because of the short muzzle, dogs may struggle with exercise and are prone to overheating, so care in hot weather is generally advised.

Conditions reported in the breed include brachycephalic airway obstruction syndrome, mitral valve disease, eye problems such as cataracts, corneal ulcers, glaucoma and tear staining, ear infections and impaired liver blood flow. Life expectancy figures range from 11 years in a 2022 UK study to 12.8 years in a 2024 UK study.

faq.a: The name comes from the Mandarin word for lion, because the dog was bred to resemble the lion of traditional Asian art. In England in the 1930s it was nicknamed the chrysanthemum dog.

faq.q: How big does a Shih Tzu get?
faq.a: A Shih Tzu should stand no more than about 27 cm at the withers. It is a small but sturdy toy breed.

faq.q: How long do Shih Tzus live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.8 years, close to the average for purebred dogs. A Japanese study found 15 years.

faq.q: How often should a Shih Tzu be brushed?
faq.a: The long double coat tangles and mats easily, so it should be brushed at least every two or three days.
